sources.title: 日本標準時
sources.publisher: 国立研究開発法人 情報通信研究機構
supports: the 1884 International Meridian Conference selected the Greenwich meridian as the prime meridian
Ordinance No. 51 of 1886 set the meridian at 135 degrees east longitude for Japanese standard time
the standard is nine hours ahead of Greenwich Mean Time
NICT currently generates and supplies Japan Standard Time

sources.title: 標準時
sources.publisher: 国立天文台 暦計算室
supports: local time based on each location's sun position preceded national standard time
railways and communications increased the need for a shared time standard
Ordinance No. 51 was promulgated on 1886-07-13 and took effect on 1888-01-01
Ordinance No. 167 of 1895 created Western Standard Time based on 120 degrees east longitude
Western Standard Time was abolished on 1937-10-01

sources.title: 日本標準時と明石市
supports: the 135-degree east meridian was designated in 1886 and the standard time system began in 1888
Akashi's meridian markers and astronomical facilities developed after the national rule was established
the present Akashi Municipal Planetarium opened in 1960

claims_policy: Dates and institutional facts are stated as reported by the listed public institutions. The episode distinguishes the legal meridian, civic symbols in Akashi, and the present-day generation of Japan Standard Time.
